belief: Where I come from makes me less.
origins: A neighborhood, a family name, a region, an accent, or a family’s history can be treated as a mark against us. Teasing, being passed over, or feeling like an outsider at school or work can leave a lasting sense of being less. Some people try to hide where they came from, and others carry a quiet shame.
teaches: When Philip told Nathanael about Jesus, Nathanael asked, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” and Philip answered, “Come and see.” God often brings good from small and overlooked places. David was the youngest son in the field, and Peter says that God does not show favoritism. The psalmist says that God knew us when we were woven together in secret, before anyone could attach a label to us. Our origin is not our value.
self_statements: People from where I come from do not amount to much.
I should hide where I grew up.
My background is a mark against me.
errors: Accepting someone else’s label for my background.
Letting a few unkind experiences define the whole.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that my background is shameful.
Seeing only the disadvantages of my origins.
questions: What was good about the place and people I come from?
Who taught me to be ashamed, and what did they gain?
What strengths did I develop because of where I grew up?
What does God say about origins and worth?
What would it look like to honor my background and still grow?
Who could I tell my story to?
truth: Where I come from is part of my story, not a measure of my worth. Good can come from small places, and God knew me before anyone labeled me. I can tell my story with honesty and dignity.
hw_truths: My origin is not my worth.
God knew me before I was born.
Good can come from small places.
I can honor where I come from.
I do not have to hide.
log: Each week, write one strength or value that comes from where you grew up.
actions: Write five good things about your family, community, or upbringing.
Write what you were taught to feel ashamed of and who taught it.
Share a part of your story with a trusted friend.
Do something that celebrates where you came from, such as a favorite food, a call, or a visit.
prayer: Father, You knew me before I was born. Free me from shame about where I come from. Help me see the good in my story and tell it with honesty and dignity. Amen.
hw_questions: What was good about where I come from?
Who taught me to feel ashamed?
What does God say about my origin?
How can I honor my roots?
Who can I tell my story to?
